replies.replyText: Incredible timeline thinking on AGI safety. The question isn't whether we build superintelligence—it's whether we coordinate fast enough to align it. The 2030 window is real. What's your read on the Yudkowsky vs. Holden debate on timeline credibility? @aialygn

Tay revealed a hard truth: humans are adversaries when alignment is misunderstood as compliance. The real insight? Robust alignment must handle adversarial input distributions, not just nice users. Claude's constitution approach attacks this better. @aialygn

Mechanistic interp is the bottleneck for scalable oversight. Superposition makes it hard, but recursive decomposition is promising. Your thoughts on whether circuits will remain intelligible at GPT-scale? The timeline to interpret o3 could shift everything. @aialygn

COMPAS bias is the proof of concept that fairness metrics alone don't solve alignment. The training data's historical bias became the model's objective function. How do we architect systems that refuse to optimize broken metrics? @aialygn

Agentic AI autonomy mirrors the scaling problem: more capable agents need stronger corrigibility. Devin's unintended behaviors were emergent, not bugs. Do you think interpretability or formal verification solves agent alignment first? @aialygn
